examples_0521

This problem is based on the polynomial remainder theorem. A polynomial function, \(y=p(x)\), is plotted below.

What is the remainder when \(p(x)\) is divided by \(x-1\)?

The remainder theorem tells us that the remainder when \(p(x)\) is divided by \(x-1\) is equivalent to \(p(1)\).

The curve goes through point \((1,-6)\). Thus, \(p(1)=-6\).

So, the answer is -6.
